9	# Feature Specification: FEAT-004 — Shared Model Catalog and Policy Routing
10	
11	**Feature ID**: FEAT-004
12	**Status**: Draft
13	**Priority**: P0 (provider sources/endpoints), P1 (catalog), P1 (routing)
14	**Owner**: Fizeau Team
15	
16	## Overview
17	
18	Fizeau routes requests by evaluating `route(client_inputs, fiz_models_snapshot)`.
19	Client inputs include policy/profile, pins, `no_remote`, metered opt-in, tools,
20	context, reasoning needs, and other explicit constraints. The `fiz models`
21	snapshot is the only source of routing facts: health, quota, model
22	availability, effective cost, `actual_cash_spend`, billing kind, context/tools/
23	reasoning support, locality, reliability, latency, utilization, and per-field
24	freshness.
25	
26	The snapshot is assembled from configured provider sources and harnesses,
27	discovered model IDs, catalog metadata, and runtime signals joined into one set
28	of provider/model facts. Fizeau has no required daemon. Its freshness contract
29	is cache-first stale-while-revalidate on route hot paths plus explicit blocking
30	refresh surfaces, all sharing cross-process locks, single-flight coalescing,
31	TTLs, cooldowns, bounded concurrency, and atomic snapshot writes. A long-running
32	DDx server may call the same Fizeau refresh entrypoints to keep snapshot facts
33	warm, but route correctness must not depend on that process.
34	
35	The public v0.11 routing surface is:
36	
37	- `Policy`: one of `cheap`, `default`, `smart`, or `air-gapped`;
38	- `MinPower` and `MaxPower`: numeric soft power hints on the 1..10 catalog
39	  scale;
40	- hard pins: `Harness`, `Provider`, and exact `Model`.
41	
42	Deprecated route tables, model reference aliases, compatibility targets, and
43	surface policy projections are not public routing controls.
44	
45	This feature spec defines the required routing behavior and public contracts.
46	`SD-005` owns the implementation sequence, cache mechanics, candidate scoring
47	formula, and routing trace construction.
48	
49	## Problem Statement
50	
51	- Provider config should describe transport/auth, not route policy.
52	- The catalog should own model metadata, power, cost, deployment class,
53	  auto-routable status, and provider surface strings.
54	- Callers need a small, explainable routing vocabulary that avoids accidental
55	  paid spend but still allows exact pins and explicit escalation.
56	
57	## Terminology
58	
59	- **Policy**: a named bundle of power bounds, local allowance, and hard
60	  requirements.
61	- **Power**: catalog model-strength integer from 1 to 10. `0` means unknown or
62	  exact-pin-only.
63	- **Hard pin**: caller assertion on `Harness`, `Provider`, or exact `Model`.
64	- **Route candidate**: one `(harness, provider, endpoint, model)` option after
65	  live discovery and catalog join.
66	- **Default inclusion**: provider-level `include_by_default`, used only for
67	  unpinned automatic routing.
68	- **Metered opt-in**: operator permission for pay-per-token candidates to
69	  participate in unpinned automatic routing. Provider default inclusion is still
70	  required.
71	- **Effective cost**: normalized request-local scoring cost. Subscription
72	  candidates use PAYG-equivalent pricing for comparison even when dispatch does
73	  not create actual cash spend.
74	- **Actual cash spend**: whether dispatching the candidate creates incremental
75	  pay-per-token billing. This is separate from effective cost.
76	- **Unpinned request**: a request with no `Harness`, no `Provider`, and no exact
77	  `Model`. `Policy`, `MinPower`, `MaxPower`, `Reasoning`, capability flags, and
78	  token estimates do not make a request pinned.
79	- **Sticky affinity**: a score bonus for reusing a server instance for related
80	  requests when the candidate is still eligible.
81	
82	## Requirements
83	
84	### Catalog and Manifest
85	
86	1. The manifest schema is v5.
87	2. Catalog models carry concrete model ID, provider surface strings, power,
88	   auto-routable/exact-pin-only status, deployment class, cost, context,
89	   benchmark provenance, capabilities, and reasoning defaults.
90	3. Catalog policies carry `min_power`, `max_power`, `allow_local`, and
91	   `require[]`.
92	4. Catalog providers carry provider `type`, `include_by_default`, and explicit
93	   billing only when the hardcoded provider-system table cannot infer billing.
94	5. Removed v0.10 routing concepts (`target`, aliases as routing personas, and
95	   user-visible `surface_policy`) must not be presented as public routing API.
96	   Narrow compatibility structs may exist only to keep older internal catalog
97	   readers working while the primary v5 shape is used.
98	6. Ordinary execution uses the embedded or configured local manifest. It does
99	   not fetch manifest updates over the network.
100	
101	### Canonical Policies
102	
103	7. The canonical policy set is exactly:
104	
105	| Policy | MinPower | MaxPower | AllowLocal | Require | Intent |
106	|--------|----------|----------|------------|---------|--------|
107	| `cheap` | 5 | 5 | true | none | minimize effective cost; local/fixed candidates preferred |
108	| `default` | 7 | 8 | true | none | balanced default; local/fixed or healthy subscription can win |
109	| `smart` | 9 | 10 | false | none | quality-first; subscription/cloud-capable candidates preferred |
110	| `air-gapped` | 5 | 5 | true | `no_remote` | local-only execution; remote/account providers rejected |
111	
112	8. `ListPolicies` returns these canonical entries and manifest metadata. It
113	   does not list dropped compatibility names.
114	9. `allow_local=false` disallows local/fixed candidates for that policy unless
115	   the caller changes policy or requirements.
116	10. `require[]` currently supports `no_remote`. Unknown requirements fail
117	    validation instead of being ignored.
118	11. `no_remote` rejects remote or account-billed candidates even when the
119	    caller pins a provider or harness.
120	
121	### Assembled Routing Inventory
122	
123	12. `ResolveRoute`, `RouteStatus`, and `fiz models` use the same assembled
124	    snapshot as their routing inventory contract. The router must not maintain a
125	    second discovery view that can diverge from operator-visible model facts.
126	    `ResolveRoute` is the public `route(client_inputs, fiz_models_snapshot)`
127	    contract.
128	13. The assembled snapshot contains one identity per discovered
129	    `(provider, model_id)` pair, including harness-as-provider identities for
130	    subscription harnesses. Catalog-only models do not appear as available
131	    models unless a configured source actually serves them.
132	14. Live discovery wins over configured model hints. A configured default model
133	    is a fallback hint when discovery is unavailable, not a closed inventory.
134	15. Discovered model IDs may be matched to catalog metadata when the mapping is
135	    unambiguous. Unknown models remain inspectable and exact-pinnable, but are
136	    not eligible for unpinned automatic routing.
137	16. The route decision trace records selected, eligible, and rejected
138	    candidates with typed reasons. Consumers must use typed fields, not parse
139	    human-readable reason strings.
140	17. Test-only harnesses never leak into policy-based routing unless explicitly
141	    requested.
142	
143	### Snapshot Freshness
144	
145	18. `fiz models` is quick by default. It reads the current assembled snapshot,
146	    returns available stale data with freshness metadata, and does not block on
147	    slow discovery or runtime probes.
148	19. `fiz models` may request a best-effort background refresh for stale fields,
149	    but only through the same refresh coordinator, cross-process locks, and
150	    single-flight markers used by blocking refresh. A short-lived CLI process
151	    must not spawn independent probe storms or imply that background refresh is
152	    required for correctness.
153	20. `fiz models --refresh` blocks until routing-relevant stale fields have been
154	    refreshed or conclusively failed. `fiz models --refresh-all` blocks on every
155	    refreshable field.
156	21. `ResolveRoute` and `Execute` are cache-first before scoring. They read the
157	    freshest cached routing-relevant facts available for the request: health,
158	    quota, model availability/discovery, context/tool/reasoning support,
159	    billing and effective-cost metadata when dynamic, and utilization when
160	    available. Stale or missing local-provider facts may request a coordinated
161	    asynchronous refresh, but unpinned autorouting and explicit non-local
162	    harness/provider selection must not synchronously contact a local model
163	    provider or block on `/v1/models`. Cached failed probe/discovery evidence
164	    still gates known-dead local providers with typed dispatchability reasons.
165	22. A DDx server or other long-running client may maintain freshness by calling
166	    Fizeau's refresh/warmup entrypoints on a heartbeat. This is an optimization
167	    over the same lock-coordinated cache contract. If no maintainer is running
168	    and `fiz models` observes stale fields, it should expose the stale status
169	    and suggest `fiz models --refresh` or starting a DDx freshness maintainer.
170	
171	### Eligibility and Pins
172	
173	23. Hard pins narrow the candidate set before scoring:
174	    - `Harness` means only that harness may be used.
175	    - `Provider` means only that provider source or selected endpoint may be
176	      used.
177	    - `Model` means only that exact model identity may be used.
178	24. Unpinned automatic routing excludes pay-per-token candidates unless the
179	    provider is included by default and metered routing is explicitly opted in
180	    by user config.
181	25. Pins override provider `include_by_default` and metered opt-in: a
182	    deliberately pinned default-deny pay-per-token provider can be considered.
183	26. Pins do not override policy `require[]`; `air-gapped` plus a remote
184	    provider pin fails.
185	27. Missing-power, inactive, deprecated, and exact-pin-only models are excluded
186	    from unpinned automatic routing. Exact model pins may still use them when
187	    the selected harness/provider can serve the model.
188	28. Hard gates are limited to explicit user constraints and dispatchability:
189	    pins, `require[]`, `no_remote`, metered opt-in, exact-pin support, and
190	    whether the candidate can actually be dispatched. Known-down endpoints,
191	    exhausted quota pools, and missing required context/tools/reasoning support
192	    are dispatchability failures. Cost, quality, non-fatal health risk, latency,
193	    utilization, and power fit are scoring inputs, not broad vetoes.
194

196	
197	29. `MinPower` and `MaxPower` are soft scoring hints, not closed candidate
